manuscript = the original typed or handwritten version of a text
publisher = a company that prepares and sells books
ghostwriter = a person who writes a book that is published under someone else's name
book signing = an event where an author signs copies for readers
literary critic = a person who writes professional judgements of books
coming-of-age novel = a novel about a young person growing into adulthood
historical fiction = a novel set in the past, mixing invented characters with real events
dystopian fiction = stories set in an imagined society that has gone badly wrong
page-turner = a book so interesting that you want to keep reading
banned book = a book that authorities have forbidden people to read or sell
commemorate = to honour the memory of a person or event
premiere = the first public showing of a film, play or work
box office = the place that sells tickets; the money a film takes
blockbuster = a very popular film that makes a huge amount of money
box-office flop = a film that fails to make much money
arthouse cinema = films made for artistic value rather than mass entertainment
film festival = an event where new films are shown and often judged
cinematography = the art of camera work and lighting in a film
screenplay = the written script of a film, including dialogue and action
film adaptation = a film based on a book, play or other work
